mainTopic: Which day a בתולה marries on, and when danger or אונס allows a different day
overview: The גמרא explains the phrase 'שקדו' with a ברייתא. A בתולה marries on Wednesday so the husband can bring a טענת בתולים to בית דין the next morning, and so he has three days to prepare the feast. The ברייתא adds three more rules: in a time of סכנה people married on Tuesday, Monday is allowed only because of אונס, and the first union is not on Friday night because of חבורה. רבה explains the 'danger': the government decreed that a Wednesday bride would first be violated by the הגמון, and modest women would rather die than submit. The גמרא explains why the חכמים did not simply teach that אונס is permitted, and why they did not cancel the Wednesday rule. A persecution is temporary, and the ruler will not bother over an uncertain Tuesday wedding. רבא explains the Monday 'אונס' as an army general coming to settle in the city, whose advance troops arrive on Tuesday. The גמרא then offers a second explanation: a death in the family after the wedding feast is already prepared.

steps.title: What does 'they were diligent' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the earlier word 'שקדו' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'they were diligent'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what a phrase mentioned earlier, 'שקדו', is talking about. This question sets up a ברייתא that will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שקדו' (the חכמים were diligent) was used earlier without full explanation. The גמרא now wants its source and meaning. The answer comes in the following steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They were diligent, they took special care

phrases.english: What is 'they were diligent'?
phrases.notes: This points back to a phrase the גמרא used earlier, about the חכמים taking special care.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and meaning of the phrase 'שקדו'.

steps.title: The ברייתא's first reason for Wednesday weddings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that a בתולה marries on Wednesday so the husband can bring a טענת בתולים to בית דין early Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Why did they say a virgin marries on Wednesday? Because if he has a claim about her virginity, he can go early to court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first explains why the wedding is on Wednesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין sat on Mondays and Thursdays. A Wednesday wedding lets the husband bring any claim to בית דין the very next morning, before he can calm down and accept the situation. This first reason will be challenged right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's claim that his bride was not a virgin

phrases.english: As it was taught: For what reason did they say
that a virgin is married on the fourth day (Wednesday)?
So that if he had a claim about her virginity,
he would go early to court.
phrases.notes: Court met on Thursday, so a Wednesday wedding means he can go the very next morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that answers the question about 'שקדו'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא about Wednesday weddings, which will lead to the phrase 'שקדו'.

steps.title: Why not marry on Sunday instead?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the wedding is not held on Sunday, since בית דין also meets on Monday morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let her marry on Sunday, and if he had a claim about her virginity he could go early to court!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reason. Sunday would also let the husband go to court the next morning, which is Monday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason 'court the next day' fits Sunday just as well as Wednesday. So that reason alone cannot explain why Wednesday was chosen. Another reason is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the week, Sunday

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שבת' means 'week', not the day of שבת. 'אחד בשבת' is Sunday, 'שני בשבת' is Monday, and so on.

phrases.english: But let her marry on Sunday,
and if he had a claim about her virginity
he would go early to court!
phrases.notes: Court also met on Monday, so Sunday seems to work just as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'court the next morning' reason for Wednesday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sunday also has a court day after it, so this reason does not single out Wednesday.

steps.title: Three days to prepare the wedding feast
steps.stepSummary: חכמים chose Wednesday for the bride's benefit, so the groom would spend Sunday through Tuesday preparing the סעודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages were diligent about the welfare of Jewish women, so that a man would put effort into the feast for three days, Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, and on Wednesday he marries her.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is the phrase 'שקדו'. חכמים wanted the groom to spend three full days preparing a proper wedding feast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Sunday wedding comes right after שבת, so there are no weekdays just before it for preparing the feast. A Wednesday wedding gives three full weekdays to prepare, which is better for the bride. This also explains the word 'שקדו' from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: He marries her, brings her into his home

steps.whatToRemember: Wednesday was chosen for two reasons: court is the next day, and the groom gets three days to prepare the feast.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁקְדוּ חֲכָמִים עַל תַּקָּנַת בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: The Sages were diligent about the welfare of Jewish women,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם טוֹרֵחַ בַּסְּעוּדָה שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים:
phrases.english: so that a man would put effort into the feast for three days:
Sunday and Monday
and Tuesday,
and on Wednesday he marries her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁקְדוּ חֲכָמִים עַל תַּקָּנַת בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Sunday challenge and explains 'שקדו'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a second reason that applies only to Wednesday.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason for Wednesday is reaching court the next day, so Sunday should work too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wednesday also gives three preparation days for the feast, which Sunday does not.

steps.title: In a time of danger, people married on Tuesday
steps.stepSummary: After a time of סכנה began, people started marrying on Tuesday, and חכמים did not object.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time of danger onward, the people adopted the practice of marrying on Tuesday, and the Sages did not stop them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a later change. Because of a danger, people moved weddings to Tuesday, and חכמים allowed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Tuesday wedding leaves only two preparation days, and court does not meet the next morning, so it is not the ideal. חכמים did not make this a rule; they only did not protest. Step 8 asks what the 'danger' was.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not protest against them

phrases.english: And from the time of danger onward
the people adopted the practice of marrying on Tuesday,
and the Sages did not stop them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a later change in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a time of danger, Tuesday weddings were accepted without protest.

steps.title: Monday is not allowed, unless forced
steps.stepSummary: Even in a time of danger one should not marry on Monday, but if there is אונס it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on Monday he should not marry. But if it is because of coercion, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets a limit. Tuesday is acceptable, but Monday is not, unless there is real force involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the danger that allowed Tuesday does not allow Monday. Only a case the ברייתא calls 'אונס' permits a Monday wedding. Steps 19–28 explain what this 'אונס' is.

phrases.english: And on Monday he should not marry.
But if it is because of coercion, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the leniency of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No Monday weddings, unless there is coercion.

steps.title: No first relations on Friday night
steps.stepSummary: The groom is kept from his בתולה bride on Friday night for the first time, because it causes a חבורה, which is forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they separate the groom from the bride on Friday night for the first time, because he makes a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with another rule. A first union with a בתולה should not be on Friday night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first union causes bleeding, which counts as making a חבורה (a wound), one of the acts forbidden on שבת. So the first union must not take place on Friday night.

keyTerms.meaning: A wound that draws blood, forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: And they separate the groom from the bride
on Friday night for the first time,
phrases.notes: He means the first union should not be on Friday night.

phrases.english: because he makes a wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first union with a בתולה is not on Friday night because of חבורה.
steps.whatToRemember: End of the ברייתא: Wednesday is ideal, Tuesday is fine in danger, Monday only by force, and no first union on Friday night.

steps.title: What was the danger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'danger' the ברייתא meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the danger?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and asks what danger made people move weddings to Tuesday. This sets up a suggestion and an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'from the danger onward' without explaining. Knowing the danger tells us why the response was only a custom change.

phrases.english: What is the danger?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the word 'סכנה' in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the danger in the ברייתא was.

steps.title: It cannot mean a death decree
steps.stepSummary: If the government decreed death for a Wednesday bride, people would drop Wednesday entirely, not just 'adopt a custom'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they decreed that a virgin married on Wednesday will be killed, would they just 'adopt a custom'? They should cancel it completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the danger was a death decree, then rejects that idea. The ברייתא's mild wording does not fit such a severe threat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Facing a death threat, the Wednesday rule would be fully cancelled, not just quietly changed by custom. The words 'נהגו' and 'לא מיחו' show it was a lighter situation. So the danger must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them uproot it, cancel it

phrases.english: If you say that they declared
a virgin married on Wednesday will be killed —
would they just 'adopt a custom'?!
Let them cancel it completely!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the danger was a death decree.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A death decree would cancel the rule fully, not lead to a mild custom.

steps.title: רבה: the הגמון decree
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the decree was that a Wednesday bride would first be violated by the הגמון, the local ruler.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: They declared that a virgin married on Wednesday must first have relations with the governor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the real answer. The government decreed that any Wednesday bride would first be taken by the ruler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is terrible but not a direct death sentence, so a custom change makes sense. Moving the wedding to Tuesday avoided the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: She will have relations, be violated

phrases.english: Rabba said: that they declared:
a virgin married on Wednesday
will first be violated by the governor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The danger was a decree that the Wednesday bride be violated by the הגמון.

steps.title: Is that danger, or coercion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא calls this 'danger' when it sounds like 'אונס' (coercion).
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this danger? It is coercion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's explanation. Being forced to submit to the הגמון is coercion, not a threat to life, so why would the ברייתא call it 'סכנה'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A forced violation is a case of אונס, not a threat to life. So the word 'danger' in the ברייתא seems not to match רבה's case.

phrases.english: Is this danger?
It is coercion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forced violation fits the word 'אונס', not 'סכנה'.

steps.title: Modest women would risk their lives
steps.stepSummary: It is called danger because some modest women would rather be killed than submit, so lives are at risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there are modest women who give themselves over to death, and they come to danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the decree does put lives at risk. Some women would resist and be killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree itself is coercion, but its result is real danger to life for women who refuse. That is why the ברייתא calls it 'סכנה'. רבה's explanation stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'danger' was the הגמון decree. It is called danger because modest women would die rather than submit, so people moved weddings to Tuesday.

phrases.english: Because there are modest women
who give themselves over to death,
and they come to danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case includes both coercion and danger to life.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הגמון decree is only coercion, so 'סכנה' is the wrong word.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some women would choose death, so the decree leads to real danger.

steps.title: Why not tell the women that being forced is permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים didn't simply teach the women that submitting under force is allowed, so they wouldn't risk their lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the חכמים teach them that when a woman is forced, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 12. If the danger is that modest women might let themselves be killed, just tell them they don't need to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12 we learned the danger comes from women who would rather die than submit to the הגמון. A woman who is forced does not become forbidden to her husband. So the חכמים could teach that rule, the women would stop risking their lives, and Wednesday weddings could stay.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them teach or publicly explain

phrases.english: But let them teach them that being forced is permitted?
phrases.notes: He means: a woman who is forced does not become forbidden to her husband, so she need not give up her life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in Step 12 by suggesting a simpler solution
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to move the wedding day because of the danger described in Step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the danger comes only from women refusing to submit, teaching them that אונס is permitted would remove the danger without changing the day.

steps.title: Some women would misuse it, and some are married to כהנים
steps.stepSummary: Teaching that rule would not work: some loose women would use it as an excuse, and wives of כהנים become forbidden even when forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are loose women, and there are also wives of כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13 with two reasons why the חכמים could not just announce that אונס is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, some loose women would go along willingly and claim they were forced, and willing relations do make a woman forbidden. Second, a כהן's wife becomes forbidden to her husband even if she was forced, so for her the rule does not help. So moving the wedding day was the real solution.

phrases.english: There are loose women,
phrases.notes: They would go along willingly and hide behind the rule, and then they really would be forbidden.

phrases.english: and there are also wives of כהנים.
phrases.notes: A כהן's wife becomes forbidden to him even if she was forced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical limitation: the suggested teaching would not solve the problem for everyone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Teaching that אונס is permitted would remove the danger.
steps.terutzMaskana: That teaching would be misused by some women and would not help wives of כהנים, so the day had to change.

steps.title: Why not cancel the Wednesday rule completely?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים didn't just do away with the Wednesday wedding rule entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them uproot it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים only allowed an exception instead of abolishing the rule to marry on Wednesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Wednesday is dangerous, why keep the rule at all? The challenge is to cancel the Wednesday rule and set a new wedding day for good.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them uproot it, cancel it completely

phrases.english: And let them uproot it!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule of the חכמים that a בתולה marries on Wednesday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge about the same danger
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's approach of only adopting a temporary custom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dangerous rule should be cancelled for good, not just set aside.

steps.title: Persecution is temporary, so the rule stays
steps.stepSummary: Decrees of persecution usually end, and the חכמים do not cancel their rules because of a passing persecution.
steps.simpleTranslation: A persecution is likely to end, and we do not uproot a rule of the חכמים because of a persecution.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 15: the danger is temporary, so the rule is only set aside for now, not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שמד is expected to end at some point. Once it ends, the original reasons for marrying on Wednesday apply again. So the חכמים let people skip Wednesday while the danger lasts but keep the rule in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Likely to be cancelled, likely to end
A rule set up by the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: A temporary danger can push aside a rule of the חכמים for now, but it does not cancel the rule forever.

phrases.english: A persecution is likely to end,
and a rule of the חכמים
we do not uproot because of a persecution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle: temporary circumstances do not cancel a lasting rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dangerous Wednesday rule should be cancelled completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stays, and people only avoid it while the persecution lasts.

steps.title: Won't the ruler just come on Tuesday too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what moving the wedding to Tuesday helps, since the ruler can simply come on Tuesday instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, on Tuesday too he will come and violate her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole idea of moving the wedding one day earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once people switch to Tuesday, the הגמון could just switch too. So it seems the move does not protect the bride at all.

keyTerms.meaning: On the third day of the week, Tuesday

steps.confusionAlert: Days are counted from Sunday: שני is Monday, שלישי is Tuesday, and רביעי is Wednesday. Don't read שלישי as Wednesday.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי נָמֵי אָתֵי וּבָעֵיל!
phrases.english: If so, on Tuesday too he will come and violate her!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי נָמֵי אָתֵי וּבָעֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a further challenge to the custom of marrying on Tuesday
steps.kashyaTarget: The custom of moving the wedding to Tuesday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ruler wants Wednesday brides, he can just as easily target Tuesday brides, so the move seems useless.

steps.title: He won't bother for an uncertain case
steps.stepSummary: The ruler will not go out of his way when he isn't sure a wedding is happening that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: For something uncertain he will not trouble himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 17: since the Tuesday wedding is not a fixed rule, the ruler can't count on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His decree was about Wednesday, the known wedding day. A Tuesday wedding is only a quiet custom, so he can't be sure a bride is marrying that day. He won't go to the trouble just in case.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'uproots himself': goes out of his way

phrases.english: For an uncertainty he will not trouble himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17 and closes this line
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: uncertainty discourages the ruler
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruler would simply move his target to Tuesday.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tuesday weddings are not fixed, so the ruler won't bother, and moving the day works.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: Monday weddings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says one may not marry on Monday, but if it is because of אונס, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on Monday he should not marry, but if it is because of אונס, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes its next line. This sets up the question about what 'אונס' means here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא allowed moving to Tuesday because of danger. Now it says Monday is normally not allowed, but there is an exception for אונס. The גמרא will need to explain what kind of אונס this is.

keyTerms.meaning: On the second day of the week, Monday
He marries, brings in the bride

phrases.english: And on Monday he should not marry,
but if it is because of the coercion, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַשֵּׁנִי לֹא יִכְנוֹס, וְאִם מֵחֲמַת הָאוֹנֶס מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the text of the ברייתא and quotes its next clause
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Monday wedding is normally not allowed, but it is permitted because of אונס.

steps.title: What is the אונס here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of אונס the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the אונס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about the word אונס in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say what the forcing situation is. The גמרא wants to pin it down.

phrases.english: What is the coercion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the clause just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What situation the ברייתא calls אונס

steps.title: It can't be the same case as the ruler's decree
steps.stepSummary: The אונס can't be the ruler's decree, because the ברייתא called that 'danger' and said people 'adopted a custom', while here it says 'אונס' and 'permitted'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is what we said before, there it calls it 'danger' and here 'אונס'! Also, there it says 'they adopted a custom', and here it says 'permitted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious answer, the הגמון's decree, and rejects it with two proofs from the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the earlier line used the word 'סכנה' while this line says 'אונס', so they seem to be different cases. Second, the earlier line said people 'נהגו', a custom, while this line says 'מותר', permitted. Different wording suggests a different situation.

phrases.english: If you say it is what we said before,
phrases.notes: He means the הגמון's decree from Step 10.

phrases.english: there it calls it 'danger',
and here it calls it 'coercion'?!
And furthermore: there 'they adopted a custom', here 'it is permitted'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to Step 20 and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects identifying the Monday אונס with the הגמון's decree
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא uses different words for the two cases (סכנה vs. אונס, נהגו vs. מותר), so they must be different situations.

steps.title: רבא: an army general is coming
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the אונס is a report that an army general is coming to the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: when people say, 'An army general is coming to the city.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question of Step 20 with a new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry here is not about the bride's body but about the wedding itself: the troops would take the food prepared for the feast. That is a loss forced on people, so it fits the word אונס, and the wedding may be moved earlier.

phrases.english: רבא said: When they say:
An army general is coming to the city.
phrases.notes: The worry is that his troops will take the food prepared for the wedding feast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, דְּאָמְרִי: שַׂר צָבָא בָּא לָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 after Step 21 ruled out the first idea
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אונס is news that an army general is coming to the city on Wednesday.

steps.title: If he is just passing through, wait
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the general is only passing through, why not just postpone the wedding?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he comes and passes through, let them delay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: a general just passing through is no reason to move the wedding earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the general only stays briefly, the family could wait until he leaves and marry the next Wednesday. So why would the ברייתא allow Monday?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case, how exactly

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he comes and passes through, let them delay!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּאָתֵי וְחָלֵיף לִיעַכַּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A short visit can be waited out, so there is no need to marry early on Monday.

steps.title: He comes to stay
steps.stepSummary: The case is a general who comes to settle in the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where he comes and stays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 23: the ברייתא is talking about a general who settles in the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the general is staying, waiting won't help, because the danger to the feast will last. So the wedding has to happen before he arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this case)

phrases.english: It is needed only where he comes and settles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general is only passing through, so waiting is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general is staying, so the wedding must happen before he arrives.

steps.title: Then why not marry on Tuesday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא allows Monday, since Tuesday is also before the general arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: At least on Tuesday let him marry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the wedding must be moved all the way to Monday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the general arrives on Wednesday, Tuesday would already be early enough. Why go two days back?

phrases.english: At least on Tuesday let him marry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case set up in Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's permission to marry on Monday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tuesday is also before Wednesday, so moving to Monday seems unnecessary.

steps.title: His advance troops arrive on Tuesday
steps.stepSummary: The general's advance troops come on Tuesday, so the wedding must be on Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: His advance troops come on Tuesday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 25 and finishes the explanation of the Monday rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general's אספרווא come a day ahead of him, on Tuesday. They would take the food just the same. So the only safe day is Monday, which is exactly what the ברייתא allows.
steps.whatToRemember: The Monday 'אונס' is an army general coming to stay; his advance troops arrive Tuesday, so the wedding moves to Monday.

phrases.english: His advance troops come on Tuesday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 and closes the explanation of the Monday clause
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a fact about the case
steps.terutzMaskana: The advance troops arrive Tuesday, so only Monday is safe.

steps.title: A second way to explain the forced situation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different explanation of 'מחמת האונס' and says it refers to the case in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: what does 'because of the forced situation' mean? It means the case taught in a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside רבא's army-general explanation for a moment and offers a new one. This line is a setup: the next step quotes the ברייתא that shows what the new explanation is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 22–26 explained 'אונס' as a general coming to settle in the city. With 'ואיבעית אימא' the גמרא opens a second, independent answer to the same question. It does not say the first answer was wrong. It just gives another way to understand the word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say…' This introduces a second, alternative answer.
'Because of the forced situation.' This is the phrase from the earlier ברייתא that we are trying to explain.
'As it was taught in a ברייתא.' This introduces a quoted ברייתא.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to רבא. 'ואיבעית אימא' simply gives another possible answer, and both answers can stand side by side.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say instead:
What is the meaning of 'due to the forced situation'?
phrases.notes: These are the words of the ברייתא that the גמרא quoted back in step 19.

phrases.english: It is as it is taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the 'אונס', running alongside רבא's army-general explanation from steps 22–26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the 'אונס' that allows a wedding on a different day?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the case described in a ברייתא, which the next step quotes.

steps.title: A death in the family when the feast is already prepared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that if the feast is ready and the groom's father or the bride's mother dies, the body is moved into a room and the couple goes right to the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose the bread was already baked, the meat already slaughtered, and the wine already mixed. Then the groom's father or the bride's mother died. In that case they move the body into a room, and they bring the groom and bride to the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that describes the new 'אונס'. Everything for the wedding is ready when a close family member suddenly dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the forced situation is a death, not a general. If the wedding waited, all the food that was prepared would go to waste. So the wedding goes ahead right away, before the burial, on whatever day it happens to be. That explains why the earlier ברייתא allows marrying on an unusual day 'because of the אונס'.

keyTerms.meaning: His bread is baked, so the feast is already prepared.
His animal is already slaughtered for the feast.
His wine is already mixed with water and ready to serve.
They move the body into a separate room.
The wedding canopy, the marriage itself.

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a very different picture of 'אונס': a sudden personal tragedy, not a threat from outside. The wedding is moved earlier because of the death, not pushed off to a later day.

phrases.english: If one's bread was baked,
and his animal slaughtered, and his wine diluted,
phrases.notes: In those days wine was served mixed with water, so 'diluted' means ready to pour.

phrases.english: and the father of the groom died
or the mother of the bride died,
they bring the deceased into a room,
and the groom and the bride to the wedding canopy,
phrases.notes: The word 'bring' carries over from the line before: they bring the couple to the חופה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the content of the ברייתא that step 27 introduced, which defines the new 'אונס'.
steps.raayaObject: The second explanation, that 'מחמת האונס' refers to a sudden death when the feast is already prepared.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the groom's father or the bride's mother dying after the wedding feast was prepared.
